transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM); Evan, Lina, Rajiv (Cobalt)

Summary (auto): Follow up on the persistent connection drops that affected prod inference endpoints; discuss mitigations and action plan. Some automatic sections omitted.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, thanks for jumping on. I'll kick off, we wanted to get a focused follow up after the outages yesterday and the intermittent reconnects you've been seeing. Evan, do you want to start with what you're seeing from your SRE side?
[00:18] Evan: Yeah thanks, I'll try to be brief. We've been seeing connection resets from the load balancer to the inference fleet, mostly during mid-day traffic spikes. It's like, connections drop, requests time out, and some clients re-try causing a thundering herd. We attached packet captures and there are a bunch of TCP RSTs and FINs, sometimes right after KV cache misses.
[00:39] Lina: One thing to note, we did a config change last week to reduce idle timeouts on the NLB to 45s to try to reduce cost, could be related.
[00:47] Jonah: Hmm, okay that is helpful. NLB idle timeout plus Redwood's own keepalive? There are a couple of interactions there; if the TCP idle is closed by NLB it can cause the server to see resets on next packet when the client re-uses connection.
[01:05] Rajiv: We're trying to avoid moving to dedicated lanes right now since budget approvals are pending, but the impact is pretty bad for some customers. We want a solid plan that doesn't require enterprise commitment straight away.
[01:18] Maya: Understood. Today we want to align on short-term mitigations you can apply, longer-term fixes on the Redwood side, and what's needed to validate. Jonah, can you walk through the probable root causes you have so far?
[01:29] Jonah: Sure. Hypothesis A: idle TCP termination on the NLB + client re-use leads to RST storms. Hypothesis B: under high concurrency the inference runtime is evicting KV entries and forcing cold starts that extend response time and cause timeouts upstream which then cascade. Hypothesis C: a rare NIC driver bug on the host that shows up under certain packet patterns — we've seen this in other cloud providers but it's uncommon.
[01:55] Evan: We have one capture where we saw a pattern: lots of late ACKs then a burst of RSTs. Also, when we routed a small percentage of traffic to another region the problem largely vanished, so that hints at something localized.
[02:12] Maya: That regionality could indicate infra-level issue, like a maintenance event or kernel driver. Did the provider open any maintenance tickets?
[02:19] Lina: They opened a ticket for packet drops but haven't linked it to our endpoints yet. We'll share the ticket.
[02:24] Rajiv: Quick ask: can Redwood provide ephemeral dedicated capacity for a soak so we can reproduce safely under identical traffic patterns?
[02:32] Maya: Yes, we can spin up a 48-hour dedicated lane in non-prod and mirror traffic. We'll send the pricing and scope; this will also help isolate provider-level vs runtime-level cause.
[02:44] Jonah: Short term mitigations: increase NLB idle timeouts back to 300s, enable application-level keepalives on the inference client (we can provide a client lib tweak), and add a circuit-breaker at the front to drop excessively retried clients. That should dampen retry storms while we investigate deeper.
[03:02] Evan: We can flip the timeout tonight, but it's a balance with connection cost. We'll do a canary on one service first.
[03:08] Priya: I'll coordinate the canary plan and make sure support is paged if it spikes. Also, we have a prebuilt playbook for circuit-breaker config we can share.
[03:18] Jonah: Great. On Redwood's side, devs will check kernel logs for NIC-level errors, SIGQUIT traces for any hung threads during eviction, and we'll run a workload that maximizes KV cache churn to try to reproduce evictions causing long tail latency.
[03:33] Rajiv: Is there any telemetry we should add on our side to make debugging faster? Specific metrics, logs?
[03:39] Jonah: Yes, please capture: per-connection drop counters, client-side socket reuse stats, KV cache hit ratio, and per-model tail latency percentiles (p95/p99). Packet captures from both sides at the same timestamps are invaluable.
[03:51] Evan: We'll add the extra metrics, packet captures should be possible. We'll need an NDA for raw captures if that matters.
[03:58] Maya: We can accept sanitized captures first. We'll share secure upload instructions. Also I'll attach our security packet and link to the private S3 for transfer.

--- Topics: immediate mitigation steps ---
[04:10] Lina: One odd observation: when the autoscaler spun new pods, we saw a ~20 second window of increased errors. Could the new pods be failing health checks and briefly dropping connections?
[04:22] Jonah: Possibly. If a pod is being cordoned and the connection draining is too short, the LB may still route traffic. We can increase drain times and pre-warm the model on start to reduce cold-start latency.
[04:34] Evan: Do you have a warmup endpoint we can call as part of pod lifecycle?
[04:38] Jonah: Yes, we can expose a quick warmup call for your deployment; it's in the docs but it's off by default for some images. We'll enable it for the soak.
[04:46] Rajiv: Also, could the client retry policy be compounding the issue? Our SDK retries aggressively.
[04:51] Priya: We saw that in earlier incidents; tuning retry backoff and adding jitter often reduces cascades.

--- Mid-call: clarifying logs and evidence ---
[05:04] Evan: I'm sharing a sample capture in the chat now. There's a block where connection count jumps and then the RSTs start. It's not consistent but frequent.
[05:12] Maya: Got it, we can look at that. Can you include the precise timestamp and request IDs so we correlate with our side?
[05:18] Evan: Yes sending those. Also sending cloud provider ticket link: https://cloudprovider.example/ticket/78910
[05:25] Lina: Provider says they had a maintenance in the same AZ but 'no customer impact' per their notice. That feels bad.
[05:31] Jonah: We'll treat that as correlated but not sufficient. We need to reproduce in a controlled soak.

--- Proposed hardened changes and roll-back criteria ---
[05:45] Maya: If we make changes (increase idle timeout, enable keepalives, tweak retry), what's our rollback criteria?
[05:51] Jonah: Rollback if error rate > 1% above baseline for 15 minutes or p99 latency increases by more than 50ms. We'll define exact thresholds in the runbook.
[05:59] Rajiv: Fine by us. Also add a step to revert any client-side retry logic if it worsens.

--- Planning validation and soak ---
[06:10] Maya: Plan: (1) tonight Cobalt increases NLB idle timeout to 300s in canary pool; (2) Redwood enables warmup and an alternative keepalive profile; (3) we spin up 48h non-prod dedicated lane to mirror traffic; (4) joint soak with packet captures.
[06:28] Evan: We'll schedule the canary at 02:00 UTC to minimize user impact. We'll also open access to the packet captures in a secure share.
[06:35] Priya: I'll coordinate calendar invites for the soak monitor window and a post-soak sync.

--- Questions from customer about security/compliance ---
[06:47] Lina: If we send packet captures, is Redwood able to handle them under our compliance constraints? We need to ensure no PII leaves the capture.
[06:55] Maya: Yes, we have a sanitized upload workflow and can sign an addendum to accept redacted captures. We'll also only ingest captures to an encrypted bucket with limited access.
[07:04] Rajiv: Also want confirmation that using ephemeral dedicated lanes won't change data residency rules.
[07:08] Maya: It will not; we can pin region and use your KMS for encryption at rest.

--- Wrap and recap ---
[07:20] Maya: Recap of next steps: Evan share captures and ticket; Cobalt will canary the NLB timeout change; Redwood will enable warmup and provide keepalive client tweak; Redwood to provision 48h dedicated soak; Jonah will run eviction-heavy test and share results. We'll reconvene after initial canary results or in three business days.
[07:45] Evan: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side? Just approval for packet capture sharing and the canary window.
[07:51] Priya: We'll follow up on approvals; I'll send the invite and the runbook draft.
[07:55] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a summary and the temporary config snippets in email. Bye all.
[08:00] End of recording.
